My two cents on ME:

ME1 was a great game that had a few minor flaws. It was a great fun and original RPG experience. The things people didn't like were game mechanics issues, like the fact that the mako was clunky, the inventory was a bit difficult to navigate, there was one combination of a gun with certain mods that let you fire forever.

ME2 fixed the minor flaws of ME1 with a sledgehammer. Mako was clucky, no more vehicles. inventory difficult to navigate, we've removed the inventory. One particular weapon/mod combo was OP, we've drastically cut the number of weapons, removed all mods and added an ammo system that doesn't make any sense. To me, the end result of all the "streamlining" was to turn it from an RPG into just a shooter.

ME3 brought it back to being more of an RPG, but was disappointing because the story kind of dropped off. I basically think it was a product of being over hyped. They had said early on that "if you play through all three games the decisions you made in the first two games will have a big impact on the third game". That was a major disappointment for most people, as nothing you do until just before the very end of the game winds up impacting how it ends.

Overall I'm glad I played the series, but it definitely has some flaws and disappointments that prevent it from being a true masterpiece.

I am going into web development as a career and with such I am actively working on a gaming news (and related content) website. I know there are a lot of them already, but my goal is to get out what gamers want and not put money first.

So my question is: as a gamer, even if you don't read gaming related news/articles/other content, what would you want in a gaming news website? Feature-wise and content-wise. I don't want to advertise, so I'll refrain from posting links, but if you have any specific questions I am more than willing to respond in a PM.
What better place to ask than /v/gaming!
I just want one with absolutely no politics. No trying to spin any console as better, no controversy because the game hurt someone's feelings, just gaming news.
Pretty much this. If the news is about the game-play, mechanics, prices, development or anything that isn't drama about the devs or the people getting butt-hurt is ok.

Couldn't agree more. Political opinion should have no bearing on reviewing the quality of the game. "Is the game fun?" should be all that matters. Just like "Is it funny?" is the final arbiter for comedians.
THIS. Absolutely. Politics and unnecessary controversy has completely trashed the gaming journalism industry in the past year or so.

This! Keep an open mind, of course one prefers a certain console over another - or PC gaming over console gaming in general - but it's important to not make it a huge deal should you intend to cover the different areas of gaming. After all we are all a big family ... nothing more annoying than different camps trying to cut eachother's throat over a silly consoler(/PC) war.

Another point which I find important is a clean design. Of course one needs to attract the eye but if it's something I dislike it's the current huge media outlets like IGN force-feeding you content, everything's flashing, vast and chaotic - at least that's how I feel about this.

Also when posting new trailers and such, try to keep high quality of the vids. No point in adding low quality vids in my opinion since we're heading towards glorious graphics at an incredible speed (not because of the ingame graphics, but rather because of the fact that screens are able to actually play stuff in 4K).

Do reviews. Make people want to return to your site and read what you have to say about a game. Some people dislike a scoring system but I do like them. Give out scores which relate to your page ... say, your page is called GameElephant, make it 6 out of 10 trunks when rating a game with actual pictures of trunks - or GameRabbit, make'em carrots and so on. I always liked when magazines or websites did this, haha. Add a TL;DR at the end listing positive and negative points. In addition to that think about adding a 'circle' for example, listing things which are neither positive or negative but simply information about the game (such as: 3rd installement of the series / other games the developer made / already announced DLCs).

Also, being up to date with your content is fine. But try to throw in an retro game now and then and review them. Like a game you liked in the past and start playing again and compare it to your past experience 10 years ago. Can it still hold up, did it age well, what new game did let itself inspire from this certain game elements and so on. Adding your own vids would be fun too. Maybe also write articles about soundtracks (of games) you liked, cool box designs or pads. Nowadays a gaming site is purely news news news ... which is informative at times but also boring. Try to celebrate your hobby and create fun content to read ... not just a bland news site with stuff you find on any other page.

In terms of pure gaming news ... try not to post every fckng little news surfacing in the internet. I find quality over quantity to be much more professional. Also, like mentioned before, keep the politics out of it ... It's one thing for example, to write about bad customer service of certain companies and appeal to your fellow gamer community to be aware - but don't bash everything and call for total desctruction. Be constructive about it and list the facts and give your comments in a well-mannered way.

Do think about if you want to have a comment system for your reviews and other contents you post on the page. Do you aim for creating a discussion or not? With all today's boards (like Voat and so on) is there a need for a comment system?

While a good functional fancy site is fun to look at, do you also aim to make your page available for mobile devices? Keep in mind that lots of people do browse the stuff they like on the way to work / on their breaks / taking a dump / waiting for an appointment and so on ... might consider put together a good mobile page as well.

Now this post kind of ended up more being an advice, haha, sorry ... if you read this post, I would like to know the address so I can peek in on occassion ... and perhaps stay for a while if I enjoy it :)

BEST OF LUCK TO YOU!

It's funny you ask this question, since lately I've been reading through old issues of Computer Gaming World for nostalgic purposes. It's funny to read an issue from '98 or '00 speculating about Duke Nukem Forever.

Truthfully I have no clue what I'd want from a gaming news site anymore.

Early access on Steam has replaced a reporter's exclusive access to previews. Many developers stay active with the community throughout the development of a game, answering questions, which further erodes the role reporters used to play. The internet has allowed publishers to go completely over a reporter's head straight to the consumers.

Reviews are hardly a thing anymore too, since most people find Let's Plays more interesting to watch and a better representation of the game. Although I still have a soft spot for a well produced video review combined with snippets of let's play footage to punctuate points.

Community sourced strategy guides have completely replaced the tips and tricks sections that used to be in magazines.

The demo disks used to be a great resource as well, frequently curating the best mods for popular games as well. But that's obsolete for obvious reasons as well. Aggregate sites tend to do a great job of filtering out the news that matters for popular mods.

All this is really making me realize that endless editorializing is practically the only thing gaming news sites have left anymore. But I hate it. I hate when reporters spend most of their time shoving their opinions down my throat.

I think a gaming media/news sites best bet is some sort of original content, or personality driven content. And mostly on youtube. Which is hard.

But even in the magazine days, I loved some of the creative features PCXL used to run, like drinking and driving games, where they all got drunk and tried to play racing games.
